subject: QuickBasket deployment-mode recommendation & pilot metrics
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@quickbasket.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@quickbasket.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: QuickBasket: follow-up from deployment call (latency/throughput)

Thanks again for the call today — helpful framing. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can decide whether to proceed with Hosted API pilot or request Dedicated capacity up front.

QuickBasket requirements (call notes):
- Checkout inference: model is a moderate-sized transformer (13B) used for product-title normalization and buy-flow suggestions.
- SLOs we care about: p95 inference latency <= 50ms end-to-end (app -> model -> return).
- Expected steady-state qps: 200 requests/sec during peak windows; we see bursts up to ~650 qps for ~3-5 minutes during promotional events.
- Payload: average prompt length ~140 tokens; responses ~60 tokens.
- Data isolation: no PHI but we need logs retained for 90 days and enterprise-grade audit logs.

Primary business question: given those numbers, do you recommend starting with Hosted API (fastest time-to-value) or reserve Dedicated capacity? We are sensitive to latency during checkout and want predictable tail behavior during promos.

Next asks from our side:
1) A short note on expected p95 and cost delta for Hosted vs Dedicated at our signal (200 sustained, 650 burst).
2) A minimal benchmark artifact we can run against to baseline both paths.
3) If Dedicated is recommended, what lead time and commitment levels should we expect?

I've attached a small CSV with a representative traffic sample (quickbasket_traffic_sample.csv). Please loop in procurement next steps if Dedicated is the right path.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, QuickBasket
elena@quickbasket.com

[attachment: quickbasket_traffic_sample.csv (CSV)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@quickbasket.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@quickbasket.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QuickBasket: follow-up from deployment call (latency/throughput)

Elena — thanks for the clear notes and the traffic sample. Short answer up front: given a p95 target <= 50ms plus sustained 200 qps and ~650 qps bursts, our recommendation is to run a short Hosted pilot first only if you can tolerate a higher chance of tail variability during burst windows. If checkout p95 is critical with strict guarantees during promos, Reserved/Dedicated capacity is the safer choice.

Key rationale and numbers (ballpark, based on similar customers and our internal bench runs):
- Hosted API (shared pools): typical observed p95 for 13B models with our optimized runtime is 55–120ms depending on concurrent contention and burst patterns. At sustained 200 qps you may see acceptable medians, but p95s can spike during noisy neighbor activity. Cost: lower up-front but potentially higher token/unit cost at peak due to queuing and autoscaling.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): we can configure a pool sized for sustained 200 qps with headroom to absorb short bursts to ~700 qps via short-term burst capacity. With Dedicated you should expect p95 in the 30–50ms range for your payloads (with KV-cache + batching tuned). Cost: higher monthly commitment (committed capacity), but predictable per-unit economics and lower variable costs at scale.

What I'd propose as a next step (safe, low friction):
1) Two-week blind benchmark run using the attached quickbasket_benchmark_template.xlsx. Goal: quantify p50/p95/p99 and token cost for Hosted vs a small Dedicated profile. I attached a template and marked the fields we need (input rates, payload shapes, runway windows).
2) Mateo/Marissa will run a Hosted baseline in our shared environment and provide a Hosted result within 4 business days once you confirm the traffic CSV is representative.
3) If Hosted results show p95 >= 65ms during your burst windows, we recommend spinning a 2-week Dedicated pilot (we can provision a trial pool with a limited commit) to validate real-world tail behavior.

Operational notes:
- Audit/log retention for 90 days and KMS support are available on Dedicated and Private; Hosted can meet 90-day retention with the enterprise package (we'll document retention SLA).
- For the Dedicated pilot we'll need approximate commit range (GPU-hours or vGPU count estimate) and a PO or MSA addendum for trial provisioning; Marissa will take point on procurement and SOW.

Attachments in this reply: quickbasket_benchmark_template.xlsx (spreadsheet with benchmark steps) and initial SOW template (SOW_QuickBasket_draft.pdf).

I'll queue a Hosted baseline run as soon as you confirm the sample is representative and we have an API key to run test traffic (we can provide a short-lived key).

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QuickBasket: follow-up from deployment call (latency/throughput)

Perfect — we'll kick off the Hosted baseline today. Concrete timeline & next steps: 
1) Hosted baseline (days 0–4): Mateo will run three traffic shapes from your CSV against Hosted; we will return p50/p95/p99, token counts, and cost estimate for 200 sustained and observed 650 burst.
2) Internal review (day 5): bench results shared with QuickBasket and joint readout call scheduled (I'll send a Calendly invite).
3) Decision gate (day 6–7): if p95 in bursts > 65ms or tail variance exceeds your acceptance criteria, Marissa will fast-track a 2-week Dedicated pilot. Estimated Dedicated trial lead time: 5–7 business days to provision after an initial commit range is agreed (we'll aim to reuse minimal MSA addendum to shorten procurement).

Action items assigned:
- QuickBasket: confirm any additional acceptance criteria Jared wants to include (checkout success rate, 95th tail for latency, acceptable error-rate).
- Redwood (Mateo): run Hosted baseline and share results by EOD Monday (2028-01-15).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare SOW addendum and provisional pricing for a 2-week Dedicated trial once the decision gate is hit.

I'll attach the Hosted baseline checklist to the calendar invite. Looking forward to the readout.

Regards,
Mateo
